pois.name: Reading Terminal Market
pois.blurb: Reading Terminal Market is an enclosed public market in Philadelphia. It opened in 1893 and remains an operating market with many independent vendors selling food, produce, prepared meals and goods.

themeConnection.text: Permanent enclosed public market opened in 1893 and still operating with independent food, produce and merchandise vendors.

pois.name: Mercat de Sant Antoni
pois.blurb: Sant Antoni Market is a large public market in Barcelona, built in the late nineteenth century. The market opened in 1882 and continues to provide food, household and other retail stalls.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered municipal market opened in 1882 and continuing as a public food and merchandise market.

pois.name: Khan el-Khalili
pois.blurb: Khan el-Khalili is a major souq and bazaar in Cairo’s historic centre. It was established in the fourteenth century and remains an operating covered market area with public shops and stalls.

themeConnection.text: Historic covered bazaar district founded in the fourteenth century and still operating as a contiguous public retail market.

pois.name: Nishiki Market
pois.blurb: Nishiki Market (錦市場, Nishiki Ichiba; literally "brocade market") is a marketplace in downtown Kyoto, located on the east end of Nishikikōji Street, one block north and parallel to Shijō Street (四条通, Shijō-dōri) and west of Teramachi Street (寺町通, Teramachi-dōri).

themeConnection.text: Named covered market street with a fixed roofed retail complex and documented market use since the early seventeenth century.

pois.name: Leadenhall Market
pois.blurb: Leadenhall Market is a covered market in the City of London. A market has existed on the site since the fourteenth century, and the present structure contains public shops and food establishments.

themeConnection.text: Named covered market occupying a fixed historic complex with origins in the fourteenth century and current public shops and stalls.

pois.name: Mercat de Santa Caterina
pois.blurb: The Santa Caterina Market is a public market in Barcelona. It was established in 1845 and has occupied the same site, although the market building was substantially rebuilt and reopened in the twenty-first century.

themeConnection.text: Named municipal covered market established in 1845 and still operating on the same historic site after rebuilding.

pois.name: St. Lawrence Market
pois.blurb: St. Lawrence Market is a major public market in Toronto. Public markets have occupied the site since 1803, while the present South Market building dates from 1845 and remains an operating food market.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered public market whose South Market building dates from the nineteenth century on Toronto’s historic market site.

pois.name: New Market
pois.blurb: New Market is a historic covered market in central Kolkata. It opened in 1874 as a municipal market and continues to operate with public shops and stalls selling food, clothing and household goods.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered market opened in 1874 and continuing as a public retail complex with food, clothing and household shops.

pois.name: Mercado Central de Atarazanas
pois.blurb: Atarazanas Market is Málaga’s municipal market. The present iron market hall dates from the nineteenth century, and the building remains an operating public market for food and everyday provisions.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered municipal market occupying a historic site and operating since the nineteenth century.

pois.name: Covent Garden Market
pois.blurb: Covent Garden has been a market site since the seventeenth century. The present market buildings form a fixed covered complex containing public shops, food businesses and market stalls.

themeConnection.text: Covered market complex with documented market origins before 1700 and continuing public retail activity in its permanent market buildings.

pois.name: Mahane Yehuda Market
pois.blurb: Mahane Yehuda Market is a permanent public market in Jerusalem. It was established in 1887 and today occupies a fixed network of covered market streets and shops selling food and other goods.

themeConnection.text: Historic permanent market complex founded in 1887 and now operating with covered streets, stalls and shops.

pois.name: Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandai
pois.blurb: Crawford Market, now officially Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandai, is a historic covered market in Mumbai. It opened in 1869 and remains an operating public market with food and merchandise vendors.

themeConnection.text: Historic covered municipal market opened in 1869 and still operating as a public retail market for food and household goods.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered public market on La Rambla, established at its present site in the nineteenth century and still operating with food stalls.

pois.name: Borough Market
pois.blurb: Borough Market is a wholesale and retail food market in Southwark, London. A market has operated on or near the present site for centuries, and the current market is a permanent covered public complex.

themeConnection.text: Operating covered food market on its historic Southwark site, documented there since the eighteenth century and housed under permanent structures.

pois.name: Spice Bazaar
pois.blurb: The Spice Bazaar is a historic covered market in Istanbul. It was completed in 1664 and continues to function as a visitor-accessible public bazaar selling spices, food, sweets and other goods.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered bazaar opened in 1664 and still operating with public food, spice and merchandise shops.

pois.name: Quincy Market
pois.blurb: Quincy Market is a historic market complex in downtown Boston. The market building was completed in 1826 and continues to operate as a public covered marketplace with food vendors and shops.

themeConnection.text: Historic covered public market hall completed in 1826 and still operating as a visitor-accessible food and merchandise market.

pois.name: Queen Victoria Market
pois.blurb: The Queen Victoria Market (also known colloquially as the Vic Market or Queen Vic) is a major landmark and public marketplace in the central business district (CBD) of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

themeConnection.text: Permanent covered and enclosed market complex founded in 1878 and still operating as Melbourne’s public retail market.

pois.name: Grand Bazaar
pois.blurb: The Grand Bazaar (Turkish: Kapalıçarşı, meaning ‘Covered Market’; also Büyük Çarşı, meaning ‘Grand Market’) in Istanbul is one of the largest and oldest covered markets in the world, with 61 covered streets and over 4,000 shops on a total area of 30,700 m2, attracting between…

themeConnection.text: Individually named historic covered bazaar established in the fifteenth century and still operating with public retail shops.

pois.name: Mercat de la Concepció
pois.blurb: The Mercat de la Concepció is one of Barcelona’s historic municipal markets. It opened in 1888 and is a permanent covered market with food shops and other everyday retail services.

themeConnection.text: Historic iron-covered public market dating from 1888 and operating as a neighborhood retail market.

pois.name: Great Market Hall
pois.blurb: The Great Market Hall or Central Market Hall, Market Hall I (Hungarian: Nagyvásárcsarnok [ˈnɒɟvaːʃaːt͡ʃɒrnok]) is the largest and oldest indoor market in Budapest, Hungary.

themeConnection.text: Large permanent covered municipal market opened in 1897 and still operating in its original Budapest location.

clue.text: A narrow roofed shopping arcade runs about 400 metres along a single street, with roughly 130 food shops; its fish-selling tradition received official permission in 1615, and its present cobblestone floor and canopy date from 1984 and 1993.

theme.title: Operating Historic Covered Markets in Cities
theme.introduction: Commerce has gathered beneath these roofs for generations. These historic covered markets remain lively centers of city life.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named permanent market hall, covered market, covered bazaar, or covered market street whose principal function is public retail trading in food, household goods, crafts, or other ordinary merchandise; (2) it has regularly operating public stalls or shops on the date of play and is ordinarily accessible to visitors during published or customary market hours; (3) the market occupies a fixed, mappable complex, building, or contiguous covered street that can be treated as one exact location; (4) the market was established, opened, or first documented at that same identifiable site on or before 31 December 1899, even if its roof or buildings were later rebuilt; (5) it lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (6) its market identity and historical date are documented or widely unambiguous from official or reputable sources.
